episodes.description: Hollis with Sunday's briefing: Poland begins national mourning after the Krakow square shooting; France says Europeans will join the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks; Saturday's French protests end in Paris clashes; New Zealand waits on special votes; U.S. forces disable a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman; Wall Street ends a rough week; and India's Taniya takes a historic beach wrestling silver in Dakar.
episodes.title: Poland Mourns, Europe Eyes Abu Dhabi, and France Counts Its Marchers

episodes.description: Hollis with Saturday's briefing: Russia hits Kyiv overnight ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks; a dedicated segment on France's protest movement, from a September high school dispute to today's Paris marches; New Zealand's election ends in a cliffhanger; Washington confirms minor strikes on Qeshm and names a new chief of staff; Wall Street closes mixed; and Swiss gold closes the jumping in Dakar.
episodes.title: Missiles Over Kyiv, France Marches Again, and a Knife-Edge Vote in New Zealand

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2008 episode: Worlds 2008 in Memphis — Antti Malin's Faeries beat Jamie Parke's five-colour control, five of the top eight wear wings, and Shuhei Nakamura makes it four straight Japanese Players of the Year.
episodes.title: Worlds 2008: Memphis and the Faeries Final

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2008 episode: Pro Tour Berlin — Luis Scott-Vargas sneaks into Sunday as the eighth seed, storms back from zero-two down in the quarterfinal, and wins an Extended top eight where six of eight decks are Elfball. (No, the famous undefeated run was a different city.)
episodes.title: Berlin: LSV and the Elfball

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2008 episode: the Faeries era — Bitterblossom, Mistbind Clique, and Cryptic Command turn a Morningtide tribal enchantment into the deck that defined a year of Standard and put five copies into the Worlds top eight.
episodes.title: Faeries: Bitterblossom's Year

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2008 episode: Shards of Alara and the birth of the mythic rare — the June 2008 announcement, one in eight packs, smaller sets, and four planeswalkers (the fifth shard's dragon waits for Conflux).
episodes.title: Shards of Alara: The Mythic Rare

episodes.description: Year sixteen: Morningtide hands Standard to the Faeries, Shadowmoor and Eventide go all-in on hybrid mana, Jon Finkel wins a Pro Tour as a Hall of Famer, Magic Online is rebuilt, and Shards of Alara splits the world into five shards and invents a whole new rarity — mythic.
episodes.title: 2008: The Year Magic Went Mythic

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2007 episode: Planar Chaos — forty-five colour-shifted timeshifted cards from alternate realities: a black Wrath of God called Damnation, a red Akroma, a green Harmonize, and the colour pie tried on inside-out.
episodes.title: Planar Chaos: The Alternate Reality

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2007 episode: Worlds 2007 at the Javits Center — Uri Peleg, the first Israeli ever to reach a Pro Tour top eight, wins the whole thing with a green-black-white Doran deck carrying both Garruk and Liliana past Patrick Chapin.
episodes.title: Worlds 2007: Doran in New York

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2007 episode: Future Sight — eighty-one futureshifted cards previewing mechanics that did not exist, and Tarmogoyf, the two-mana lhurgoyf that became contemporary shorthand for a fifty-dollar bill.
episodes.title: Future Sight: The Future Leaked Early

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2007 episode: Lorwyn in full — how loyalty works, why the five were delayed out of Future Sight, the eight tribes underneath them, Thoughtseize, and why five rare cards in a set with no humans rewired the whole game.
episodes.title: Lorwyn: The Planeswalkers Arrive

episodes.description: Year fifteen: Planar Chaos bends the colour pie, Future Sight leaks mechanics from Magic's future — and one two-mana creature whose type line names a card type that does not exist yet — Tenth Edition turns the core set black-bordered, and Lorwyn changes the game forever with five planeswalkers.
episodes.title: 2007: The Year the Planeswalkers Arrived

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2006 episode: Dissension completes Ravnica — Azorius, Rakdos, and Simic take the stage, the guild split cards arrive, graft and hellbent and forecast debut, and Terry Soh's Invitational card Rakdos Augermage finally prints.
episodes.title: Dissension: Ten Guilds, Complete

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2006 episode: Coldsnap — the third Ice Age set designed in about six weeks and released ten years after Alliances, retroactively replacing Homelands in the block, with snow mana, ripple, and recover.
episodes.title: Coldsnap: The Lost Set That Never Was

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2006 episode: Worlds 2006 at the Carrousel du Louvre — Makihito Mihara, the only Dragonstorm player in the Standard rounds, beats Ryo Ogura in an all-Japanese final, while Wafo-Tapa's Dralnu du Louvre becomes the deck the event is named for.
episodes.title: Worlds 2006: Dragonstorm in Paris

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2006 episode: Time Spiral in full — the first bonus sheet, one hundred twenty-one timeshifted reprints in old frames and purple symbols, suspend and split second, and a block built entirely out of the game's memory of itself.
episodes.title: Time Spiral: The Past in Every Pack

episodes.description: Year fourteen: Ravnica's last four guilds arrive in Guildpact and Dissension, a spoiler lawsuit opens the year, Coldsnap completes the Ice Age block a decade late, and Time Spiral turns the game's own past into a set — then Makihito Mihara storms Paris with the only Dragonstorm deck in the room.
episodes.title: 2006: The Year Magic Turned Back the Clock

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2005 episode: Betrayers of Kamigawa — ninjutsu sneaks its first creature onto the battlefield, and Umezawa's Jitte, a two-mana equipment so strong it warped every format it touched, becomes a legend of its own.
episodes.title: Betrayers of Kamigawa: Ninjas and the Jitte

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2005 episode: Worlds 2005 in Yokohama — Katsuhiro Mori and Ghazi-Glare, Japan's team title on home soil, Kenji Tsumura's Player of the Year, and the first Hall of Fame class: Finkel, Kastle, Hovi, Comer, and Råde.
episodes.title: Worlds 2005: Japan's Sweep and the First Hall of Fame

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2005 episode: March 2005 — Wizards bans eight cards from Standard in a single announcement, all six artifact lands plus Arcbound Ravager and Disciple of the Vault, and closes the book on the most lopsided era in the game's history.
episodes.title: The Affinity Bans: Eight Cards in One Day

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2005 episode: Ravnica in full — a city the size of a world, four guilds in the first set and ten across the block, hybrid mana's debut, dredge, the shocklands, and Dark Confidant, Bob Maher's Invitational card at last.
episodes.title: Ravnica: Ten Guilds, One City

episodes.description: Year thirteen: the ban hammer ends the Affinity era — eight cards in one day, six of them artifact lands. Kamigawa closes with ninjas and the Jitte. Ninth Edition is the last white-bordered set. And Ravnica rebuilds the game around guilds, hybrid mana, and shocklands on the way to a Japanese sweep at Worlds in Yokohama.
episodes.title: 2005: The Year Magic Found Its Guilds

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2004 episode: Unhinged — the silver-border sequel six years in the making, with fractions, gotcha, a card you tear up, and a foil-only secret hiding in the basic lands.
episodes.title: Unhinged: The Joke Set Returns

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2004 episode: Worlds 2004 at Fort Mason — fifteen-year-old Julien Nuijten beats Affinity in the final with green-white Astral Slide, sets a prize record, and headlines the first Worlds top eight with no American in it.
episodes.title: Worlds 2004: The Fifteen-Year-Old Champion

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2004 episode: Champions of Kamigawa and the great rules gamble — the legend rule rewritten so rival legends destroy each other, flip cards, splice, and a block built on eighty legendary creatures.
episodes.title: Champions of Kamigawa: The Legend Rule

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2004 episode: Darksteel in full — indestructible and modular debut, and the story of Skullclamp, a one-mana equipment that drew two cards per corpse until the first Standard ban in five years stopped it.
episodes.title: Darksteel and Skullclamp: The One Toughness That Broke Standard

episodes.description: Year twelve: Darksteel arms Affinity with Skullclamp, the Ravager, and the Vial; Champions of Kamigawa rewrites the legend rule and bets a block on legendaries; Unhinged brings back the joke sets; Gabriel Nassif takes Player of the Year without winning a Pro Tour; and a fifteen-year-old wins Worlds in San Francisco.
episodes.title: 2004: The Year Affinity Ate Magic

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2003 episode: Worlds 2003 in Berlin — Daniel Zink and Jin Okamoto both sleeving up Mirari's Wake for the final, and the United States taking the team title.
episodes.title: Worlds 2003: The Wake Mirror in Berlin

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2003 episode: Scourge closes the Onslaught block and debuts storm — the mechanic Mark Rosewater would call the most broken ever designed — plus the first You Make the Card winner, Forgotten Ancient.
episodes.title: Scourge and Storm: The Mechanic That Broke Counting

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2003 episode: Eighth Edition and the most visible change in Magic's history — the 2003 card frame redesign, what changed, why players fought about it, and why it stuck.
episodes.title: The New Card Frame: Magic Gets a New Face

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2003 episode: Mirrodin in full — the artifact world, equipment's debut, affinity and imprint, the artifact lands, and the block that quietly loaded the gun Affinity would fire.
episodes.title: Mirrodin: The World Made of Metal

episodes.description: Year eleven: Legions fields an all-creature set, Scourge unleashes storm, Eighth Edition gives the game a brand-new face for its tenth anniversary, and Mirrodin rebuilds the world out of metal — equipment, affinity, and all. Kai Budde wins his seventh Pro Tour, and Daniel Zink takes Worlds in a Berlin Wake mirror.
episodes.title: 2003: The Year Magic Turned to Metal

episodes.description: Episode twenty-eight: Leo and Vera settle making up after a real argument — a towel bar loose for twelve days, an hour of quiet that turns into a contest, saying the true small thing without grading the apology, leaving last month in last month, and making up before supper because nothing tastes right when somebody's passing the potatoes with feelings, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: Making Up Before Supper

episodes.description: Episode twenty-seven: Leo and Vera settle company's coming — Leo hears six guests and tries to make it ten, Vera's short rule of a clean bathroom, a place to sit, and hot food on time, the serving bowl exiled to the top of the washing machine, a one-pot menu fuss over a second meat settled by freezer sausages, and the rule that nobody cleans alone while company is in the house and both hosts sit down at their own table, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: Company's Coming

episodes.description: Episode twenty-six: Leo and Vera settle keys on the hook — Leo's driveway sword speech handing the truck keys to their oldest and the dented tailgate from backing into their own mailbox, Vera's three short rules (text when you get there, gas back to where you found it, keys on the hook every time), trust given in steps, honesty about a scare on the road earning more room instead of trouble, the younger one watching as a preview of her own turn, and saying the trust out loud, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: Keys on the Hook

episodes.description: Episode twenty-five: Leo and Vera settle keeping the spark in a long marriage — tall roses that scared the cat versus one song on the kitchen radio with the burner turned low, a truck warmed up without an announcement, a shirt button sewn back in silence, and the rule of one small deliberate thing a day, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: Slow Dancing in the Kitchen

episodes.description: Episode twenty-four: Leo and Vera settle what's for supper — Leo's anything's fine that secretly means steak and a hmm that's a no wearing a hat, Vera's two-choice rule and the pencil list on the fridge, chicken thawed since breakfast, one-taste gravy quality checks, and phones in the other room so supper is where the day gets told, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: What's for Supper?

episodes.description: Hollis with Wednesday's briefing: Democrats win both the House and Senate in the midterms, flipping Senate seats in Texas, Kansas and South Carolina; Iran's Revolutionary Guard claims four tankers hit mines near Hormuz, a claim not independently verified, as talks with Washington remain far apart; Ukraine's aid-centre death toll rises to thirty-seven and Russia strikes power stations in Kyiv and Zhytomyr; Spain's transport minister resigns after two deadly train crashes; President Trump says American aid to Israel will end at the end of the year; Wall Street closes mixed; and Kenya wins a historic rugby sevens gold in Dakar.
episodes.title: Democrats Take Congress, Hormuz Tanker Claims, and Kenya's Historic Gold

episodes.description: Hollis with Tuesday's briefing: American officials say the United States carried out limited defensive strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island as a draft deal circulates after the Doha talks; Russia launches a sweeping barrage on Ukraine's power grid a day after a bombing killed at least twenty-six people at an aid distribution point, and the Kremlin confirms peace talks in Abu Dhabi next week; Americans vote in the midterm elections; oil rebounds after a sharp fall; and the Dakar Youth Olympic Games continue in Senegal.
episodes.title: Strikes on Qeshm, a Barrage Over Ukraine, and Election Day

episodes.description: Hollis with Monday's briefing: Iran's Revolutionary Guard claims two tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz as talks continue in Doha; Ukraine says Russia used the Oleshky ceasefire to reinforce its positions; more than fifty-four million Americans have already voted on the final day of campaigning before the midterms; Bangladesh garment factories reopen as wage protests continue; oil falls more than four percent; and the Dakar Youth Olympic Games continue in Senegal.
episodes.title: Tankers in Hormuz, Oleshky Questions, and Election Eve

episodes.description: Episode twenty-two: Leo and Vera settle putting the house to bed for winter — two lists over two afternoons instead of one heroic day, Leo's gutters, hoses, straight-stacked woodpile and truck check outside, Vera's dated furnace filter, soup-stocked pantry and labeled bins inside, the patio cushions in the Christmas-lights bin, and a traded walk-through with no hovering, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: Putting the House to Bed for Winter

episodes.description: Hollis with Sunday's briefing: Russian strikes cut power to hundreds of thousands in Ukraine while Ukrainian drones damage a Russian industrial site, and Pope Leo hopes the Oleshky truce could spur broader peace efforts; Iran sets out its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz within two days; more than fifty-two million Americans have already voted in a record early midterm turnout; Bangladesh forms a wage board as garment protests continue; Binance resumes withdrawals after covering ninety-five percent of the stolen tokens; and the clocks fall back as daylight saving time ends.
episodes.title: Power Cuts in Ukraine, Hormuz Conditions, and a Record Early Vote

episodes.description: Episode twenty-one: Leo and Vera settle the project that took three trips — a new porch light and a fixed back step, three hardware-store runs for cracked wire nuts, a wrong candelabra-base bulb, and dead drill batteries, Vera's muffin tin of sorted screws, a photo of the wires and a pen label for the breaker, Leo's ladder and heavy work, a fridge list before the keys come out, and a third-trip ice cream tax, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: The Project That Took Three Trips

episodes.description: The World Briefing launches with Hollis: Iran's supreme leader warns of a response without geographic limits while diplomats work to reopen the Strait of Hormuz; the U.S. approves a 2.1 billion dollar Patriot missile sale to Ukraine; hackers steal 6.3 billion dollars from Binance in the largest crypto theft on record; Congo's Ebola deaths pass five thousand; the midterms enter their final weekend; Wall Street posts its worst day since June; and Senegal opens the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics, Africa's first Olympic event.
episodes.title: Hormuz Tensions, a Record Crypto Heist, and Africa's First Olympics

episodes.description: Episode twenty: Leo and Vera settle the grocery run together — Vera's twenty-two-item list in store order, Leo's marked-down brisket wild card that turns into a Sunday smoker supper, chips hidden under the bread, one long checkout conversation with Denise, and the settled rule that the list is law with one wild card each, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: The Grocery Run Together

episodes.description: Episode nineteen: Leo and Vera settle Halloween at their house — Leo's extension cords, orange lights and a fog machine Vera vetoes, a scarecrow in his second-best flannel, Vera's candy count with the bowl inside and door duty split in turns, and the leftover rule, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: Halloween at Our House

episodes.description: Episode eighteen: Leo and Vera settle the sick rules — Leo outvoted by a thermometer at one hundred and one, Vera's soup and medicine times in the kitchen notebook, Leo's one blanket and total confidence when Vera was down last winter, and four signed rules for when the well one becomes the entire staff, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: When One of Us Is Sick

episodes.description: Episode seventeen: Leo and Vera settle the junk drawer — Vera counts four in the house, Leo defends a takeout menu as a shim and three mystery keys, a super glue that glued itself shut, the picture hooks that saved supper last month, and a treaty that leaves one drawer honestly mysterious, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: The Junk Drawer

episodes.description: Episode sixteen: Leo and Vera settle the truck noise — nine days of cold-start chirping Leo covered by turning the radio up, Vera's dated log in the kitchen notebook and a shop quote already in the folder, Leo's hood-up diagnosis of a cracked belt and low steering fluid, and a new rule that a noise gets said out loud within twenty-four hours, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: The Truck Is Making a Noise

episodes.description: Anniversary special: Leo and Vera celebrate Wes and Rachel's twentieth anniversary — what makes their marriage work, what makes Leo and Virgo last long-term, and today's horoscopes for both signs.
episodes.title: Twenty Years: What Makes Leo and Virgo Last

episodes.description: Episode fourteen: Leo and Vera settle the Thanksgiving war room — Vera's mother sends a three-page schedule in October with the gravy timed to the minute and arrival times for them in their own house, the seating chart that exiled Leo to the loud talkers, Vera's phone call that moves the invasion from seven to ten and puts her mother on rolls and pies, and Leo's turkey on the smoker outside, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: The Thanksgiving War Room

episodes.description: Episode thirteen: Leo and Vera settle helping in the kitchen without taking it over — three peeled potatoes held up for credit, a soup burner that was set low on purpose, the colander exiled to the top of the fridge, and a kitchen treaty on the fridge door, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: Helping Is Not Taking Over

episodes.description: Episode twelve: Leo and Vera settle the Saturday sleep-in — Vera's one morning not up first running the house, Leo up at six thirty with the sun, the leaf blower loophole in the nine o'clock mower treaty, and trash cans carried down the driveway like suitcases, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: Who Gets to Sleep In?

episodes.description: Episode eleven: Leo and Vera settle the road trip rules — Leo drives by feel and takes the locked-gate shortcut, Vera runs the route, the cooler and the two-mile exit warning, with one unplanned stop, a forty-minute gas station stop, and Dale who restores tractors, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: The Road Trip Rules

episodes.description: Episode ten: Leo and Vera settle the holiday map — Leo wants his mama's meatloaf and big table first, Vera defends a rotation so both mothers feel chosen, with early phone calls, labeled leftover containers, and Leo's one-recliner clause, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: Whose House First?

episodes.description: Episode nine: Leo and Vera settle the thermostat war — Leo comes in hot from the yard wanting sixty-nine, Vera defends seventy-two as a budget line with buttons, and the treaty that ends it: seventy-two by day, seventy by night, no unannounced edits, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: The Thermostat War

episodes.description: Commander Academy — Ellis and Theo build a kitchen-table interaction suite: how many answers a deck actually needs, spot removal, board wipes, counterspells, and protection, and the Debtors' Knell test for cutting narrow cards.
episodes.title: Commander Academy #6: The Interaction Suite - Removal, Counterspells, and Protection

episodes.description: Episode eight: Leo and Vera settle the great chore chart debate — who does what around the house, Leo's dishwasher art form versus Vera's laminated chart, the loud jobs with an audience and the invisible jobs of noticing, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: The Chore Chart

episodes.description: Episode seven: Leo and Vera on running the money together — one pot, one checkbook, nothing split, Leo's grand-gesture spending impulses versus Vera's ledger and lists, the three buckets and the fun-money rule, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: One Pot: Running the Money Together

episodes.description: Episode six: Leo and Vera on gifts — Leo's big premiere presentation versus Vera's researched, useful, noticed-it-months-ago gift, the budget-and-wishlist compromise, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: Gifts: Big Versus Useful

episodes.description: Episode five: Leo and Vera on meeting each other's friends — Leo working the room versus Vera's briefing and quiet research, the earn-your-place translation, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: Meeting the Friends

episodes.description: Milo and Jax run the pre-draft war room for Wes's third Reality Fracture draft, tonight at Cardtropolis in Silverdale: the blue seat map from Seventeen Lands, all four of the set's counterspells by name, the card truths that move picks, an autopsy of the one-and-two draft from October fifteenth, and a seven-point checklist for the table.
episodes.showName: Pack One, Pick One · Milo & Jax
episodes.title: Draft Three at Cardtropolis: The Expert Tune-Up

episodes.description: Episode four: Leo and Vera settle who plans the date — Leo's grand night out versus Vera's itinerary with parking and a backup plan, the one-booked-anchor compromise, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: Who Plans the Date?

episodes.description: Episode three: Leo and Vera decode Leo-Virgo texting — the Leo triple text versus the Virgo draft folder, a translation guide for capital letters, periods and reply times, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: The Texting Rules

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2002 episode: Worlds 2002 in Sydney — Carlos Romão, the Latin Alliance, and the smiling Psychatog that ate the world, three games to two.
episodes.title: Worlds 2002: Romão and Psychatog

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2002 episode: Torment in full — the beautiful, dangerous gamble of building an entire set around black, and Judgment's green-white answer.
episodes.title: Torment: The Black Set

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2002 episode: the June 24, 2002 launch of Magic Online — Leaping Lizard, set redemption, a leaked set list, and the night Magic moved onto the internet for good.
episodes.title: Magic Online: The Game That Never Closes

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2002 episode: Onslaught's fetchlands — five quiet lands that changed deckbuilding forever, one life and a search at a time.
episodes.title: The Fetchlands: Fixing Forever

episodes.description: Year ten: Torment tilts the block black and Judgment answers, Magic Online launches and puts Magic on the internet for good, Onslaught brings morph, tribal, and the fetchlands, and Carlos Romão's Psychatog smiles over Sydney.
episodes.title: 2002: The Year Magic Went Face-Down

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2001 episode: a design deep dive into flashback — the mechanic that taught spells to live twice, straight from the graveyard.
episodes.title: Flashback: Playing Spells Twice

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2001 episode: Worlds 2001 in Toronto — Tom van de Logt's Machine Head outlasts the merfolk lock, and the tour's first top eight disqualification.
episodes.title: Worlds 2001: Van de Logt in Toronto

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2001 episode: Odyssey in full — a new continent called Otaria, the Mirari, threshold, and the graveyard becoming a second hand.
episodes.title: Odyssey: The Graveyard Era

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2001 episode: Apocalypse in full — the Legacy Weapon fires, Urza and Gerrard fall, Yawgmoth dies, and enemy colors finally get their painlands.
episodes.title: Apocalypse: Yawgmoth Falls

episodes.description: Year nine: Planeshift and Seventh Edition arrive, Kai Budde has his unstoppable year, the Weatherlight saga ends in Apocalypse as Yawgmoth falls, Tom van de Logt takes Worlds in Toronto, Deckmasters pits Garfield against Finkel, and Odyssey opens Otaria — the graveyard era begins.
episodes.title: 2001: The Year the Saga Ended

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2000 episode: a design deep dive into Invasion's toolbox — kicker's optional costs, split cards' two spells in one, and domain's reward for going wide on colors.
episodes.title: Kicker and Split Cards: Invasion's Toolbox

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2000 episode: after Urza's broken block, design pulled power way back — rebels, mercenaries, rhystic spells, and the real cost of playing it safe.
episodes.title: The Masques Hangover

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2000 episode: Worlds 2000 in Brussels — Jon Finkel versus Bob Maher Jr., two Tinker decks, and a final widely called the greatest ever played.
episodes.title: Worlds 2000: Finkel and the Greatest Final

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 2000 episode: Invasion in full — the Phyrexian invasion of Dominaria, the coalition that rose to meet it, and the roaring return of gold multicolor cards.
episodes.title: Invasion: The Gold Invasion

episodes.description: Year eight: Friday Night Magic is born, Nemesis and Prophecy close the Masques block, Jon Finkel beats Bob Maher Jr. in the Brussels final called the greatest ever played, Peter Adkison leaves the company he founded, and in October Invasion brings gold cards roaring back as the Phyrexians invade Dominaria.
episodes.title: 2000: The Year Magic Went to War

episodes.description: Yokohama, August 1999: the Cologne friends' payoff. Nineteen-year-old Kai Budde storms the Top 8 with a mono-red artifact machine, sweeps the shortest final ever played, and closes the decade as World Champion and Player of the Year.
episodes.title: Worlds 1999: Kai Budde and the Twenty-Minute Final

episodes.description: After Combo Winter, R&D built a set that could not break anything: rebel chains, Cateran mercenaries, spellshapers and a tax-collecting port — while the Weatherlight crashed onto a city of masks where everything is for sale.
episodes.title: Mercadian Masques: The Power-Down

episodes.description: April 1999: Magic tore its rulebook down to the studs — the stack replaced the batch, interrupts died, combat damage went on the stack, and Summon became Creature. The biggest rules change in the game's history, up close.
episodes.title: Sixth Edition: The Rules Rebuild

episodes.description: The autopsy of a broken season: how Memory Jar and Megrim forced the first emergency ban in Magic history, and how the DCI spent 1999 banning its way back to sanity, card by card.
episodes.title: Combo Winter: The Emergency Ban

episodes.description: Year seven: Combo Winter deepens as Memory Jar forces the first emergency ban in the game's history, Sixth Edition rebuilds the rules around the stack, Urza's Destiny finishes the block, Hasbro buys Wizards, the Weatherlight crashes on Mercadia — and Kai Budde takes Worlds in Yokohama.
episodes.title: 1999: The Year the Bill Came Due

episodes.description: The enchantment block that Urza hijacked: Tolarian Academy, the free spells, Yawgmoth's Will and Morphling — how the most powerful set ever printed launched Combo Winter and the December bans.
episodes.title: Urza's Saga: The Power Set

episodes.description: The silver-bordered joke set of August 1998: B.F.M., Blacker Lotus, Ashnod's Coupon and denimwalk — plus the serious legacy smuggled inside: the first tokens in booster packs and Christopher Rush's full-art basic lands.
episodes.title: Unglued: Autopsy of a Joke

episodes.description: Seattle, August 1998: a star-packed Top 8, Ben Rubin's second final of the year, and seventeen-year-old Brian Selden winning the World Championship in his Pro Tour debut with Cali Nightmare.
episodes.title: Worlds 1998: Selden and the Schoolboy Champion

episodes.description: The Rath cycle's final two sets: Gerrard learns Volrath is his blood brother, the crew storms the Stronghold and escapes through Ertai's portal, Mirri falls, and Exodus quietly reinvents how every card shows its rarity.
episodes.title: Stronghold and Exodus: The Rescue and the Escape

episodes.description: Year six: the Weatherlight crew storms Volrath's Stronghold and escapes Rath at a terrible price, Jon Finkel wins his first Pro Tour, seventeen-year-old Brian Selden takes Worlds in Seattle, Unglued prints the game's first full-art lands, and Urza returns with a school, a golem, and the most broken set ever made.
episodes.title: 1998: The Year Urza Came Back

episodes.description: Deck review special — Ellis and Theo break down a custom Golgari Food commander deck.
episodes.title: Rachel Ward, Louisiana Swamp Witch

episodes.description: Deck review special — Ellis and Theo break down a custom Azorius draw-engine commander deck.
episodes.title: Wesley Ward, Master of Many Paths

episodes.description: Milo and Jax talk Reality Fracture draft — what to pick early, which colors are open, and the traps to avoid.
episodes.showName: Pack One, Pick One · Milo & Jax
episodes.title: Reality Fracture Draft Deep Dive

episodes.description: The full Commander Academy series in one listen — building from scratch, upgrading precons, and rookie mistakes. All four parts stitched together.
episodes.title: Commander Academy: The Complete Guide

episodes.description: Series premiere: Leo (a Leo) and Vera (a Virgo) break down why Leos and Virgos keep dating each other, the compliment-versus-correction translation guide, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: Why We Keep Dating Each Other

episodes.description: Series premiere: Walter (playing since month one) and Maya (Commander-era convert) start a year-by-year trip through Magic history. 1993: Richard Garfield, Gen Con, Alpha, the Power Nine, ante, Chaos Orb, and Arabian Nights, the first expansion ever.
episodes.title: 1993: The Year It All Began

episodes.description: Year two: Antiquities brings the Brothers' War, Revised rotates the Power Nine out forever, Legends introduces gold cards and legendary creatures, and Zak Dolan wins the first World Championship by actually sideboarding. Plus The Dark, Fallen Empires, and the first restricted list.
episodes.title: 1994: The Year Magic Grew Up

episodes.description: History of Magic's first special: the full story of Arabian Nights — Garfield's solo design, the purple-and-gold card back that almost happened, the scimitar symbol, the accidental Mountain, and the cards (Library of Alexandria, Bazaar of Baghdad, Juzam Djinn, Shahrazad) still echoing today.
episodes.title: Arabian Nights: The First Expansion — Deep Dive

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 1994 episode: Legends in full — first gold cards, first legendary creatures, the five Elder Dragons and the road to Commander, and the booster-box collation disaster.
episodes.title: Legends — Deep Dive

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 1994 episode: Antiquities and the Brothers' War in full — Urza vs Mishra, the Sylex Blast, Mishra's Workshop and the Urza lands, and the 2022 set that returned to the story.
episodes.title: Antiquities — The Brothers' War, Deep Dive

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 1994 episode: the first World Championship in full — 512 open-entry players at Gen Con, Zak Dolan's singleton control deck vs Bertrand Lestree's Channel-Fireball beatdown, and the sideboarding lesson that still holds.
episodes.title: The First World Championship — Zak Dolan, Deep Dive

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 1994 episode: a double feature — The Dark's gothic tone, Blood Moon and Maze of Ith, paired with Fallen Empires' Hymn to Tourach, thallids and thrulls, and the great overprinting lesson.
episodes.title: The Dark and Fallen Empires — Deep Dive

episodes.description: Year three: Standard is created, Fourth Edition goes worldwide, Ice Age becomes the first standalone set with Necropotence and Brainstorm, Chronicles triggers the reprint crisis behind the Reserved List, Alexander Blumke wins Worlds in Seattle, and Homelands closes the year.
episodes.title: 1995: The Year Magic Stood Alone

episodes.description: Episode two: Leo and Vera settle who apologizes first in a Leo-Virgo relationship — the Leo grand gesture versus the Virgo three-paragraph essay, a three-step apology formula, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: Who Apologizes First?

episodes.description: Milo and Jax walk through Wes's real Reality Fracture draft: the full fifty four card pool, all fourteen cuts graded, his final forty, a recommended forty with two swaps — Unsummon over Countersculpt, Twinned Vision over Sphinx's Approach — and the opening hand verdict. Keep, and bottom Denzilore.
episodes.showName: Pack One, Pick One · Milo & Jax
episodes.title: Your Draft, Graded: A Reality Fracture Walk-Through

episodes.description: Milo and Jax grade Wes's second Reality Fracture draft from his pack one pick one — Garruk, Veiled Butcher over Wrath of the Bloodmane and Saheeli — through the full pool: two mythics, seven removal spells, zero fixing lands. Their forty: blue-black control splashing four red spells, with all fifteen cuts explained.
episodes.showName: Pack One, Pick One · Milo & Jax
episodes.title: Garruk First Pick: Another Draft, Graded

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 1995 episode: Ice Age in full — the first standalone set, snow and cumulative upkeep, slow cantrips and Brainstorm, Necropotence, and the cards the whole game still orbits.
episodes.title: Ice Age — Deep Dive

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 1995 episode: Chronicles, the white-bordered reprint set that crashed the crown jewels, split players from collectors, and made a certain famous promise inevitable.
episodes.title: Chronicles: The Reprint Crisis — Deep Dive

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 1995 episode: Worlds 1995 in Seattle — Blumke's Rack Control, Hernandez's creatureless Vise prison, the locked-deck rule, and the first team title.
episodes.title: Worlds 1995: Blumke and the Hymn Deck — Deep Dive

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 1995 episode: Homelands with love and honesty — Ulgrotha, Feroz and Serra, Baron Sengir, why the set was so weak, and its strange beloved afterlife.
episodes.title: Homelands: The Worst Set Ever (With Love) — Deep Dive

episodes.description: Commander Academy — Ellis and Theo break down mana bases using Rachel's Food deck, from budget taplands to optimized fixing.
episodes.title: Commander Academy #5: Mana Bases - From Budget Taplands to Optimized Fixing

episodes.description: Year four: the Pro Tour launches in New York with real prize money, the Reserved List makes last year's promise official, Necropotence owns the summer, Tom Chanpheng wins Worlds in Seattle with a deck he registered wrong, Alliances closes the Ice Age story with Force of Will, and Mirage sails to a whole new continent.
episodes.title: 1996: The Year Magic Turned Pro

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 1996 episode: the first Pro Tour in full — Skaff Elias's idea, the five-cards-from-every-set format, a Land Tax mirror in the final, Michael Loconto's Millstone deck, and the third-place Necro deck that ate the summer.
episodes.title: The First Pro Tour — New York, Deep Dive

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 1996 episode: the Reserved List — the reprint policy published March 4, 1996, what the promise covered, the Chronicles-shaped hole in it, and why it still shapes prices and formats thirty years later.
episodes.title: The Reserved List — The Promise, Deep Dive

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 1996 episode: Alliances in full — the eight-month wait after Homelands, the Ice Age team's last word, pitch spells and Force of Will, and the strongest small set of the early game.
episodes.title: Alliances — Deep Dive

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 1996 episode: Mirage in full — the Menagerie playtesters, Jamuraa and the Mirage War, phasing and flanking, the tutor cycle, and Lion's Eye Diamond's terrible first impression.
episodes.title: Mirage — Deep Dive

episodes.description: Year five: Visions closes the Mirage War, Fifth Edition prints the biggest set in game history and cuts Lightning Bolt, Wizards buys Dungeons and Dragons, Mike Long beats his own deck in Paris, Portal teaches a generation, the Weatherlight Saga sets sail, Jakub Slemr wins Worlds in front of ESPN2 cameras, and Tempest changes the weather.
episodes.title: 1997: The Year Magic Set Sail

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 1997 episode: Fifth Edition in full — the 449-card giant, the pruning philosophy, the three buckets of cuts, the new art, and the twelve-year exile of Lightning Bolt.
episodes.title: Fifth Edition — Deep Dive

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 1997 episode: Weatherlight and the start of the Saga — Ryan and Rosewater plot Magic’s first great storyline, the Legacy, the crew of the skyship, and the story told on the cards.
episodes.title: Weatherlight: The Saga Begins — Deep Dive

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 1997 episode: Worlds 1997 in Seattle — ESPN2 cameras, the mixed-format marathon, Jakub Slemr’s Four Color Black, Canada’s team title, and the champion nobody picked.
episodes.title: Worlds 1997: Slemr and the Four-Color Black — Deep Dive

episodes.description: History of Magic special, follow-on to the 1997 episode: Tempest in full — Rosewater’s first lead design, Garfield’s return, Rath and Volrath, slivers, shadow, buyback, the licid lesson, and the cards that would not leave.
episodes.title: Tempest — Deep Dive

episodes.description: Milo and Jax grade Wes's live Reality Fracture Arena draft pick by pick: the red/white removal-first pool, three Emberlings, three Graft Surgeons, the Voxmancer hybrid fight, three Wes challenges that flipped the coaching, the two-Tomik damage amplifier, and a build that ditched the auto-added Swamps. Draft A-, build A-.
episodes.showName: Pack One, Pick One · Milo & Jax
episodes.title: Three Emberlings Deep: A Pick-by-Pick Draft, Graded

episodes.description: Milo and Jax deliver the one-month state of the union on Reality Fracture, hours before Wes's paper draft at Cardtropolis: fresh Seventeen Lands numbers show the pair standings frozen with blue on top and Simic in the basement, the great first-wave deflation (Crusher normalizes, the empower family splits, the Kitesail saga resolves), the sleepers the room still gives away (Unsummon is a top-three common), the traps with receipts (the planeswalker-conditional duals, Divining Duelist, Wrecking Gecko), and the paper-pod playbook for tonight.
episodes.showName: Pack One, Pick One · Milo & Jax
episodes.title: Reality Fracture, One Month In: State of the Union

episodes.description: Episode one: Nora and June break down how the Holocaust unfolded as a process — from legal exclusion and the Nuremberg Laws in the nineteen thirties, to ghettos, the mass shootings of nineteen forty-one, and the killing centers, to resistance, liberation, and why the early steps still matter.
episodes.showName: The Holocaust, Broken Down · Nora & June
episodes.title: It Didn't Start With the Camps.

episodes.description: Milo and Jax prep Wes for tonight's All Leylines Eve chaos draft at Cardtropolis — every pack from a different Standard-legal set, twenty-plus sets in the pool — and every player starts the game with a Leyline of Anticipation in play, so every spell in every hand has flash. The corrected episode: forget the axe from the first cut. Sorcery bombs and big creatures go up, haste and the word instant go down, discard on the draw step, disenchant as leyline assassination, and the land-pass, act-last sequencing that wins when the whole table plays at instant speed.
episodes.showName: Pack One, Pick One · Milo & Jax
episodes.title: All Leylines Eve: Everything Has Flash

episodes.description: Episode twenty-three: Leo and Vera settle the great fridge clean-out — a nine-day meatloaf in a foil hat, Vera's name-and-date tape and three-day leftover rule, Leo's nine-drop hot sauce bottle and two senior-citizen pickles, forty sauce packets in the butter door, and one earned rescue supper, plus today's horoscope for both signs.
episodes.title: The Great Fridge Clean-Out

episodes.description: Precon Upgrade Lab #1 - Ellis and Theo open Wes's own Family Matters precon (Zinnia, Valley's Voice): what's genuinely good stock, the first ten cuts, and rebuilds at $25, $50, and $100 leaning into 1-power ETB creatures and token payoffs.
episodes.title: Precon Upgrade Lab #1: Family Matters - Upgrading Zinnia

episodes.description: Milo and Jax deliver sealed-first prep for Star Trek prerelease weekend: artifact removal goes way up with Borg and Spacecraft density, how to evaluate Spacecraft and station your crews, the ten archetypes a sealed pool can actually be - Borg's deep commons, Dilemma's common payoffs, the black-red sacrifice trap, Strange New Worlds' absurd ceiling - and the benchmarks to hit before chasing a bomb splash: roughly five removal, seventeen lands, and a real two-drop count.
episodes.showName: Pack One, Pick One · Milo & Jax
episodes.title: Set Phasers to Sealed: Star Trek Prerelease Prep

episodes.description: Hollis with Thursday's briefing: Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi remain too close to call, with Democrats already holding fifty-four seats; Iran's Revolutionary Guard says two tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, and South Korea plans to move its naval unit closer to the strait; Ukraine's aid centre death toll rises to forty-two; the Bank of England raises rates for the first time since twenty twenty-three; New Zealand heads to a dead-heat election on Saturday; Wall Street rallies as Brent falls below one hundred dollars; and a photo finish in Dakar leaves two triathletes sharing bronze.
episodes.title: Two Senate Races Still Open, Fires in Hormuz, and a Bronze Too Close to Split

episodes.description: Hollis with Friday's briefing: Ukraine's aid centre toll rises to fifty-three and overnight strikes cut power in seven regions; Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi remain too early to call; Iran exempts ships from India, China, Iraq and Qatar in Hormuz; more than three thousand migrants are rescued in the Canary Islands in six days; New Zealand votes Saturday in a dead-heat election; Wall Street falls sharply with the Nasdaq in correction; and Kenya's Rising Lionesses return home with Youth Olympic gold.
episodes.title: Ukraine Toll Rises to Fifty-Three, Hormuz Exemptions, and Kenya's Lionesses Come Home
